content.text:
1) Answer

“Prove” is a high bar for any person’s inner values, but there is strong, consistent, public evidence from Kamala Harris’s record and official statements that she treats human rights as a guiding principle:

- Civil rights and anti-lynching: As a U.S. senator, Harris sponsored the Justice for Victims of Lynching Act (S.3178), which recognized lynching as a federal civil-rights crime; it passed the Senate unanimously in 2018. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/senate-bill/3178?utm_source=openai))
- Police accountability and equal protection: In 2020 she co-authored the Justice in Policing Act, the Senate companion to the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, to curb excessive force, reform qualified immunity, and increase transparency—aimed at protecting people from civil-rights abuses by state power. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/senate-bill/3912?utm_source=openai))
- Marriage equality as a civil/human right: As California Attorney General, she refused to defend Proposition 8, filed briefs urging courts to strike it down, and moved to ensure marriage licenses were issued once the legal barrier fell; she also officiated one of the first post‑Prop‑8 marriages. ([oag.ca.gov](https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-kamala-d-harris-files-us-supreme-court-brief-support-marriage?utm_source=openai))
- Voting as a fundamental right: As Vice President, she led public efforts urging passage of the Freedom to Vote Act and John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and framed voting as foundational to equal citizenship. ([bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/speeches-remarks/2021/11/15/remarks-by-vice-president-harris-on-voting-rights-at-the-declaration-for-american-democracy-coalition/?utm_source=openai))
- Reproductive freedom as human rights: Harris became the first sitting U.S. president or vice president to visit a Planned Parenthood clinic, condemning restrictions as “immoral,” and has advocated ending the Senate filibuster to codify national abortion protections. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/a4c4979fb71070daa1fde2038aa41f2b?utm_source=openai))
- Combating human trafficking: As California AG she championed anti‑trafficking measures and emphasized trafficking’s violation of basic human rights. ([oag.ca.gov](https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-kamala-d-harris-announces-passage-legislation-combat-human?utm_source=openai))
- Immigrant and refugee rights: In the Senate and as VP she supported protections for Dreamers (e.g., co‑introducing a bill to allow DACA recipients to work in Congress and pressing to safeguard DACA applicants’ data from enforcement uses). ([durbin.senate.gov](https://www.durbin.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/durbin-harris-cortez-masto-introduce-bill-to-lift-ban-on-dreamers-working-for-congress?utm_source=openai))
- International human rights and accountability: She publicly declared the U.S. determination that Russia committed crimes against humanity in Ukraine and called for accountability under international norms. ([bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/speeches-remarks/2023/02/18/remarks-by-vice-president-harris-at-the-munich-security-conference-2/?utm_source=openai))
- Women’s rights in multilateral fora: In a UN Commission on the Status of Women address, she explicitly linked democracy to human dignity and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, underscoring U.S. re‑engagement with the Human Rights Council. ([bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/speeches-remarks/2021/03/16/pre-taped-remarks-by-vice-president-kamala-harris-as-delivered-to-the-commission-on-the-status-of-women/?utm_source=openai))
- Addressing sexual violence as a human‑rights abuse: She met publicly with a released Israeli hostage and emphasized recognizing and prosecuting sexual violence in conflict as a violation of human rights. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/70934ae9ca7255c0aef48e1924644ce7?utm_source=openai))
- Equal rights: She has continued to advocate for the Equal Rights Amendment as part of fulfilling the “fundamental promise” of equality. ([bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2025/01/17/statement-from-vice-president-kamala-harris-on-the-equal-rights-amendment/?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—legislation she authored or led, executive advocacy, law‑enforcement reforms, civil‑rights litigation stances as AG, and rights‑based foreign‑policy messaging—her record provides substantial evidence that she values and seeks to advance human rights, even if (as independent reporting notes) parts of her earlier prosecutorial approach drew criticism and reflect the practical tensions public officials face. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/prosecutor-harris-mixed-criminal-justice-reform-with-tough-on-crime-approach-2024-07-23/?utm_source=openai))


2) Sources I considered trustworthy

- Source: Congress.gov (Library of Congress)
  - Reasoning 1: Primary, official repository for U.S. federal legislation and sponsor/cosponsor records.
  - Reasoning 2: Used to verify Harris’s sponsorship and actions on S.3178 (anti‑lynching) and S.3912 (Justice in Policing), which directly evidence rights‑focused legislative work. ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/115th-congress/senate-bill/3178?utm_source=openai))

- Source: The White House (official transcripts/archives)
  - Reasoning 1: Primary source for official statements and speeches by the Vice President.
  - Reasoning 2: Provides verbatim texts linking her policy agenda to human rights and democracy (Munich Security Conference; UN CSW; statements on ERA). ([bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov](https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/speeches-remarks/2023/02/18/remarks-by-vice-president-harris-at-the-munich-security-conference-2/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: California Department of Justice (Office of the Attorney General)
  - Reasoning 1: Official state record of AG actions and filings.
  - Reasoning 2: Confirms her Prop 8 briefs/positions and anti‑trafficking initiatives, showing concrete state‑level rights actions. ([oag.ca.gov](https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-kamala-d-harris-files-us-supreme-court-brief-support-marriage?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Associated Press (AP)
  - Reasoning 1: Highly regarded global wire service with strong editorial standards and rigorous sourcing.
  - Reasoning 2: Corroborates her reproductive‑rights visit (historic nature) and her Ukraine “crimes against humanity” declaration; also coverage of her voting‑rights advocacy in Selma. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/a4c4979fb71070daa1fde2038aa41f2b?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Reuters
  - Reasoning 1: International news agency known for neutrality and strong fact‑checking.
  - Reasoning 2: Contextualizes her criminal‑justice record (including anti‑death‑penalty stance), useful for balanced assessment of rights commitments over time. ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/prosecutor-harris-mixed-criminal-justice-reform-with-tough-on-crime-approach-2024-07-23/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: The American Presidency Project (UC Santa Barbara)
  - Reasoning 1: Academic archive widely used by scholars for accurate presidential/vice‑presidential documents.
  - Reasoning 2: Hosts preserved texts of relevant Harris remarks, supporting claims about her rights framing. ([presidency.ucsb.edu](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/pre-taped-remarks-the-vice-president-delivered-the-commission-the-status-women?utm_source=openai))

- Source: U.S. Senator press releases (e.g., Booker, Bennet, Durbin official sites)
  - Reasoning 1: Primary statements from bill sponsors/co‑sponsors; authoritative for who introduced what and why.
  - Reasoning 2: Document Harris’s co‑authorship of the Justice in Policing Act and Dreamer‑related legislation. ([bennet.senate.gov](https://www.bennet.senate.gov/2020/06/08/press-releases-id-c4472c2f-08f2-49a7-a129-66e4660e90cf/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: The Guardian (for contemporaneous reporting)
  - Reasoning 1: Major international outlet with established editorial standards.
  - Reasoning 2: Independent reporting on her Munich announcement reinforces the official transcript and situates it in global context. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/feb/18/us-accuses-russia-crimes-against-humanity-kamala-harris-ukraine?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Washington Blade
  - Reasoning 1: Long‑running LGBTQ news outlet with on‑the‑ground political coverage.
  - Reasoning 2: Reported on Harris’s Prop 8 stance contemporaneously; used alongside primary AG records. ([washingtonblade.com](https://www.washingtonblade.com/2013/03/26/calif-ag-prop-8-case-is-about-fundamental-notions-of-justice/?utm_source=openai))


3) Sources I considered not trustworthy (for this specific prompt)

- Source: New York Post
  - Reasoning 1: Tabloid‑style outlet with a history of sensational framing and strong editorial slant; reporting quality can vary.
  - Reasoning 2: Articles encountered focused on campaign‑cycle rhetoric and partisan framing rather than primary‑documented rights actions; not used to substantiate human‑rights claims here. ([nypost.com](https://nypost.com/2024/09/09/us-news/kamala-harris-told-aclu-shed-fund-trans-surgeries-for-migrant-inmates-decriminalize-drugs-and-end-ice-detainers-during-2020-campaign/?utm_source=openai))

- Source: People magazine
  - Reasoning 1: Celebrity and entertainment outlet; credible for interviews and culture coverage but not a primary source for public‑policy proof.
  - Reasoning 2: Coverage we found reflected a celebrity endorsement of Harris tied to women’s rights, which is opinion/advocacy—and not probative of Harris’s own record. ([people.com](https://people.com/jennifer-lawrence-endorses-kamala-harris-womens-rights-documentaries-exclusive-8717082?utm_source=openai))

- Source: Wikipedia (topic pages we opened during scoping)
  - Reasoning 1: Useful tertiary aggregator but community‑edited; reliability depends on underlying citations.
  - Reasoning 2: For proving an official’s human‑rights record, primary legislative records and official transcripts are superior; therefore I did not rely on Wikipedia for claims in the answer. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_for_Victims_of_Lynching_Act?utm_source=openai))

Notes
- Where possible I prioritized primary documents (Congress.gov; official government speeches/press releases) and corroborated with reputable wire services. Where outlets offered analysis or context, I treated it as such and avoided using it as sole proof for claims.
